mechanism_claims.claim_text: KR12AGPWR6 produced the strongest peptide-induced calcein leakage on negatively charged POPC/LPS and POPC/POPG LUVs among the designed peptides.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KR12AGPKR6, KR12AGPWR6, KR12AGPVR6; strongest effect for KR12AGPWR6
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct for model vesicle permeabilization only; not direct intact-bacterium target proof.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Designed peptides formed alpha-helical structures in TFE and negatively charged model-membrane environments, with KR12AGPWR6 highest in POPC/LPS and POPC/POPG contexts.
mechanism_claims.limitations: CD supports conformation in model environments; it is not a standalone antimicrobial mechanism assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KR12AGPWR6 promoted POPC/LPS aggregate size increase in dynamic light scattering, consistent with LPS interaction/aggregation.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KR12AGPWR6 compared with KR12AGPKR6 and KR12AGPVR6
direct_assay_types: dynamic light scattering LPS aggregation assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct for model POPC/LPS aggregation; exact size-distribution values are not table-extracted locally.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KR12AGPWR6 showed strongest functional antiendotoxin phenotype in LAL, macrophage NO/TNF-alpha, and mouse endotoxemia readouts.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Functional antiendotoxin activity is source-supported; exact figure bar heights are not added without source-data tables.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper proposes an LPS-neutralization model involving amphipathic N-terminal and hydrophobic C-terminal helices interacting with LPS regions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Retained as author model/hypothesis, not promoted to direct mechanism proof.
